name: 86_render_ssfr_anisotropic_kernel
_comment: SSFR anisotropic kernel (Yu & Turk 2013 ellipsoid splats, docs/todo/PLAN_ssfr_anisotropic_kernel.md). Off by default; on, the depth/thickness passes ray cast per-particle ellipsoids computed by Phantom::Physics::computeAnisotropy. Distinct from the bilateral 'Anisotropic Smoothing'.

steps.label: Liveness check
Precondition: the anisotropic kernel is off by default
Precondition: default kernel settings (k_r = 4)
DFSPH at the default (stable) scale
A 7x5x7 block (spacing 2.0) so there are interior, surface and edge particles
Container walls
Rebuild fluid
Precondition: sane, non-zero seed count
Let the block slump so the surface is irregular
Synthetic cube map for SSFR reflections
Shared directional light
Turn on screen-space fluid rendering
A few frames with sphere sprites
Precondition: with the kernel off, SSFR draws sphere sprites
Screenshot: sphere sprites (baseline)
Turn the anisotropic kernel on
Change: the kernel reports on
A few frames with ellipsoid splats
Change: SSFR now ray casts ellipsoids
Change: one ellipsoid per fluid particle
Change: some neighbourhoods are large enough for the PCA
Change: surface particles are stretched (mean sigma_max/sigma_min > 1)
Record the CPU cost (not asserted beyond sanity)
Screenshot: ellipsoid splats
Depth-only view of the ellipsoid splats
Advance a frame
Screenshot: raw ellipsoid depth
Back to surface mode
Retune while paused: k_r = 1 forces spheres (no Step -- the paused-recompute path)
Let one frame run the recompute
Change: k_r = 1 makes every kernel a sphere
Restore k_r
Turn the kernel off again
Advance a frame
Change: back to sphere sprites
Invariant: particle count conserved through the kernel toggles
Invariant: the app is still alive
Neg: k_r below 1 is rejected
Neg: an unknown kernel param is rejected
Neg: a malformed kernel param is rejected
Neg: a non-boolean kernel toggle is rejected
Neg: an unknown kernel stat is rejected
